# Node-local model cache

Status: built, behind `agent.nodeModelCache.enabled` (default off). Scope: `internal/modelcache`,
`internal/webhook/node_model_cache.go`, `internal/agent/node_model_cache.go`, `cmd/nvsnap-helper/modelcache.go`.

## 1. Problem

Without a shared model volume ([helm-shared-model-volume.md](helm-shared-model-volume.md)), every cold pod
downloads its model into a fresh `emptyDir` that is deleted with the pod. On a 4-pod multi-node instance on GB300
(November 2026, nvsnap build not recorded, [results/NODE-MODEL-CACHE-2026-11.md](../results/NODE-MODEL-CACHE-2026-11.md)), each pod downloaded 1.56 TB, and the download inits
ran 30 to 32 minutes (their start and end times). A restore is not affected: it skips the download (section 3).
Every first cold start of a function version, and every redeploy, pays the download again, for every pod.

## 2. What it does

A cold pod seeds its download volume from a copy on its node's disk, or one the agent fetches from a peer node,
instead of downloading. After a real download, the agent keeps a copy. The pod's own volumes and its main container
do not change, and any problem with the cache falls back to the pod's own download.

| Case | What fills the pod's volume |
|---|---|
| A complete copy of the same download on this node | The copy, every file checked against its manifest while it is copied |
| A copy on another node | The agent fetches it while the init waits (at most `agent.nodeModelCache.wait`), then as above |
| No copy anywhere, a corrupt copy, a failed fetch, no room | The pod's own download, unchanged; the agent then keeps a copy |

Without single flight, the first instance's pods still each download. With it (`agent.nodeModelCache.singleFlight`,
[model-cache-single-flight.md](model-cache-single-flight.md)), one pod downloads and the others stream its download.

## 3. Why restores do not change

- The main container still mounts its original `emptyDir`. Only the download init mounts the cache, read-only.
- A capture still finds the download volume unused by any dumped process, so a group restore still skips the
  download init.
- Nothing that is serving or checkpointed mounts the cache, so evicting a copy cannot touch a running or captured
  process.

## 4. Design

**Key.** A download's key is a hash of:

- the tenant of the pod's namespace;
- the model identity and its layout in the volume (`modelid` `ShareKey`);
- the download init's image;
- its command and arguments;
- its env in declared order, except the platform's per-instance metadata (`GROVE_*`, `NVCF_*`, `KUBERNETES_*`,
  `HOSTNAME`, `OTEL_*`), which would split every redeploy's key. A field reference to the pod's own identity (its
  name, namespace, uid, node or addresses) is keyed by its path, so it does not split the key: a download whose tree
  depended on it could not be shared at all;
- its `envFrom` sources in order (the last one wins);
- its volume mounts, each with its volume's full source;
- the pod's and the init's security contexts (`fsGroup` and the users decide the owners a download leaves).

A Secret or ConfigMap whose content changes under the same name is the same recipe.

A download init that can read a label or an annotation of its pod, by an env field reference or through a
downward-API volume it mounts (plain or projected), is not cached (`readsLabelsOrAnnotations`): their values can
differ between pods of one recipe and change after admission, and the key could not tell the trees apart. The
platform's per-instance variables (the `GROVE_*`, `NVCF_*` and other names the key leaves out) are exempt: every
function's download init reads its labels and annotations through them, and they do not steer what it writes.

Admission and the agent both compute the key from the pod spec and the namespace (`ResolveModelCacheDownload`). The
agent never takes it from the label admission sets: a pod that labels itself with another key is ignored.

**Layout on the node.** One directory per key under `agent.nodeModelCache.root`:

| Path | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `<key>/gen-<id>/tree/` | the files |
| `<key>/gen-<id>/MANIFEST` | every entry's path, type (file, directory, relative symlink), mode, size and sha256 |
| `<key>/gen-<id>/.complete` | written last, after the tree is synced |
| `<key>/.attempt-<id>/` | a harvest or fetch in progress, mode 0700 |

A generation is immutable once complete. A new copy is always built in an attempt directory and renamed into place,
so no directory anyone has mounted is replaced.

**Admission** (`nodeModelCachePatches`) wraps the download init in `nvsnap-helper model-cache`. It mounts
`<root>/<key>` read-only into that init only, and labels and annotates the pod with the key, the volume and the init.
It wraps an init only when all of these hold:

- The pod is a cold pod: the restore and election branches of admission did not take it. A pod stamped with
  `nvsnap.io/restore-from` whose hash restores nothing (no capture yet, or a CRIU capture not restored) is a cold
  pod too.
- The pod already uses the node's nvsnap bundle, because the gpushare library is placed. The helper comes from the
  same bundle, so a pod that did not depend on the bundle does not start to. A volume the pod declares under the
  helper's name counts only if it is a `hostPath` to the bundle; from anything else, the init is left unwrapped.
- The init mounts its download volume whole, with no `subPath`.
- No restartable sidecar (an earlier init with `restartPolicy: Always`) mounts the download volume read-write. Such
  a sidecar runs beside the download and the engine, so the volume would not hold only the download's tree.

Any other volume the init can write and a later container reads might be an output that a seed would not produce.
Admission cannot tell, so it passes each one to the helper with `--watch`. The helper fingerprints these volumes
before and after the download; a download that changed one is not cached.

**The helper**, in the init:

1. If the volume already has content, a restarted init, it runs the download, which knows how to continue.
   Copies run 8 files at a time: a model of a terabyte and more, in shards of gigabytes, copies at disk or network
   speed only with several streams. The same holds for a peer fetch.
2. If a complete generation exists, it copies it in, checking each file's size and sha256 as it copies. On any
   mismatch it empties the volume and runs the download.
3. It waits only while the agent's fetch heartbeat (`<key>/.incoming`) is fresh, and never past `wait` seconds.
4. Otherwise it runs the download unchanged, and passes its exit code through.

It reports `seeded` or `downloaded` as the init's termination message. After a download it adds the tree's
fingerprint: a hash of the volume root and every entry's path, type, size, mode, owner, mtime, change time and link
target, over at most 500,000 entries. The change time is what makes the fingerprint hold against a writer: any write,
`chmod` or `chown` sets it, and no unprivileged call sets it back, as one can an mtime. A runtime that relabels the
volume's files when the main container starts would change every change time; the agent then keeps nothing (it logs
the mismatch) and pods download as before.

A seed gives every entry, and the volume itself, its recorded owner, mode (special bits included) and mtime. If the helper runs as root, it
sets any owner. If not, every entry must belong to the helper's own user, as when the download ran as that user;
otherwise it refuses before writing and the pod downloads. The cache's own copies are readable by any user.

**The agent** (`nodeModelCache`) looks at the pods on its node every 10 s:

- **Sources.** Every 5 minutes the agent makes the ConfigMaps match its disk, which repairs a registration that
  failed. A ConfigMap left with no source is deleted.
- **Fill.** For a pod whose init has not finished and a key the node does not have, it fetches the key from a peer
  listed in the ConfigMap `nvsnap-model-cache-<key>`, over the agent HTTP API, while refreshing the heartbeat. Every
  file is checked against the peer's manifest. The copy is published and the node listed as a source only after all
  files pass. A peer is dialed at its node's `InternalIP` on the agent port (`peerAgentURL`), as every agent-to-agent
  feature does. With `agent.hostNetwork=false` nothing listens there (no `hostPort`), so peer fetches fail and pods
  download; this is a limit of the shared peer resolver, not of the cache.
- **Harvest.** For a pod whose init exited 0 and a key the node does not have, it copies the pod's `emptyDir` from
  the host into a new generation, hashing as it copies. It publishes the copy only if its fingerprint is the one the
  init reported, so a file the engine removed, added or rewrote after starting is never cached. A download that
  reported no fingerprint is not kept.
  - The walk opens every file before copying any, then copies `Parallel` (8) files at a time from those
    descriptors. After each copy the file's size, mtime and change time must still be those the walk saw, so a
    shard rewritten in place, even with its mtime set back, is refused. Unlinking a file changes it too, so a pod
    torn down mid-harvest (as the originals are once a capture's restore replaces them) leaves nothing kept; the
    next cold start downloads and harvests again. A harvest normally ends long before that: on a 1.56 TB model on GB300 it
    took about 5.5 minutes, and the engine took about 13 more to load (November 2026, nvsnap build not recorded,
    [results/NODE-MODEL-CACHE-2026-11.md](../results/NODE-MODEL-CACHE-2026-11.md)).
  - The walk never follows a symlink anywhere in a path. Each entry is opened through its parent's descriptor and
    checked to be the entry examined, so a workload that swaps a directory for a symlink mid-walk cannot lead the
    agent out of the volume. A FIFO or device is refused without blocking.
- **One attempt per key at a time.** A node runs one attempt per key, and each attempt has its own directory.
  Attempts left by an earlier agent are removed at start, before any new attempt begins; never by age.
- **Disk.** Before an attempt, the agent reserves its allocation against `maxPercent` of the filesystem: each file
  rounded to 4 KiB, plus 4 KiB per entry. It counts complete generations by allocated blocks, plus other
  reservations, keeps 10% of the filesystem free, and refuses trees of more than 500,000 entries. If room is short it evicts the least
  recently used keys first. A key used by a pending or running pod on the node, or busy with a fill, harvest or
  transfer, is never evicted. The node is removed from a key's sources before its files go.

## 5. Failure handling

| Failure | Result |
|---|---|
| Corrupt or missing cached file | The helper's copy fails its checksum; the pod downloads |
| Peer serves bytes that do not match its manifest | The fetch is discarded; the next peer is tried; with none left, the key is not fetched again for 10 minutes |
| Agent restarts during a fetch | The heartbeat goes stale; waiting inits download; the attempt is removed at the next start |
| Download init fails | Nothing is harvested |
| A file changes, or the pod is torn down, during a harvest | The harvest is discarded; the next cold start downloads and harvests again |
| Disk short | The attempt is skipped; the pod downloads as before |
| Feature off, or auth not required | The webhook does not wrap inits; the agent does not start the cache |

## 6. Security

- The peer routes `/v1/model-cache/...` serve one tenant's models to any authenticated agent. The agent turns the
  cache off unless `--auth-mode=required`, and the chart refuses to render it otherwise.
- No token reaches a customer pod. The cache is mounted read-only into the download init only.
- File requests are confined to the generation's tree.
- Keys are tenant-scoped and computed by the agent, as above.

## 7. Sizing

Put `root` on the node's largest local filesystem, ideally the one the kubelet keeps pods' `emptyDir` volumes on.
The first production-sized model measured was 1.56 TB per pod (a 4-pod GB300 instance, November 2026, nvsnap
build not recorded, [results/NODE-MODEL-CACHE-2026-11.md](../results/NODE-MODEL-CACHE-2026-11.md)). Its download
ran at about 870 MB/s per pod, so a copy only beats it if it runs at several GB/s. The default 30% of a 4 TB image
disk is too small for such a model; the agent then keeps nothing and says why (`not harvesting ... no room within the
budget`).

## 8. Not built

- **Cross-node deduplication of the first download** is single flight, a separate design and switch
  ([model-cache-single-flight.md](model-cache-single-flight.md)).
- **RDMA transfer.** The fetch uses the agent HTTP API, one stream per file.
- **Checksums on checkpoint fetches.** Those still check size only; this cache checks sha256 on every copy.
